headline: Gut microbiome variants, networks and metabolites linked to host phenotype and disease
label: Gut Microbiome Host Association
summary: Cohort-scale PheWAS, interpretable graph networks and gut-disease databases make microbiome-host links testable and reusable across phenotypes and diseases.
synthesis: The common thread is linking gut microbial features to host phenotype and disease, with attention to reusable resources. A microbiome-wide PheWAS tests 12.8M microbial SNVs against 244 host phenotypes in 10,781 people, yielding 940 associations and a public summary-statistics catalogue. A preprint applies graph neural networks to individual association networks from HMP2/iHMP metagenomes and identifies a co-abundant Bacteroidales module driving IBD prediction. A structural equation framework integrates large microbiome cohorts with smaller paired microbiome-metabolome datasets to build microbiome-metabolome-disease pathways. GutBiomeDB and gutDBase consolidate microbiome and transcriptomic data, with gutDBase spanning 175 datasets and 15 gut-related diseases. The new element is strain-level variant association and cross-dataset integration, not one shared method.
